summary: LLM API costs are exploding even as per-token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, with enterprise spend passing $8.4 billion in 2025 and on track to double again. Inference-time optimization—combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, output control, and monitoring—can realistically cut production LLM bills by 50-80% with no loss in output quality. The highest-leverage lever is prompt caching, which can reduce input token costs by up to 90% on repeated prefixes with byte-identical model output.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Prefix Caching)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG context, few-shot examples) so cached tokens are billed at a steep discount and skip recomputation. The single highest-leverage, lowest-risk cost lever in 2026—now shipped natively by every major provider.
techniques.savings: 41-90% reduction on cached input tokens; 13-31% faster time-to-first-token
techniques.example: Place your 20,000-token knowledge base and fixed system prompt at the very start of every request so the static prefix stays byte-identical; Anthropic bills cached reads at ~10% of the normal input price. Avoid putting dynamic tool results inside the cached prefix, which can paradoxically raise latency.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Embeds incoming queries and returns a stored response when a semantically similar prior query exists (above a cosine-similarity threshold), eliminating the entire LLM call rather than just discounting input tokens. Complementary to prompt caching.
techniques.savings: 30-50% fewer total requests (typical 45% cache hit rate in chatbots/FAQ workloads)
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to match 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset steps' to the same cached answer, skipping the API call entirely for the second query.

techniques.name: Model Routing (Tiered Model Selection)
techniques.description: Routes each query to the cheapest model capable of handling it—budget-tier models for simple tasks, flagship models only for hard reasoning—using a classifier or rules engine. Flagship-to-budget pricing differences reach 16x for identical token counts.
techniques.example: Route 70% of queries to GPT-4o-mini and 25% to GPT-3.5-class models, reserving GPT-4-class for the 5% that need deep reasoning—dropping a $3,250/month chatbot to under $400.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by stripping redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, and using compression models (e.g., LLMLingua) to shorten context while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run system prompts and retrieved RAG chunks through Microsoft's LLMLingua-2 to drop ~30% of tokens with negligible quality change before sending to the API.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Caps generated tokens via max_tokens, explicit instructions, and structured/JSON output. Output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens on flagship models, so constraining them is disproportionately impactful.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Answer in under 3 sentences, JSON only' instead of letting the model emit a verbose 600-token explanation.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously (within 24h) at a flat discount across all requests.
techniques.example: Send nightly document-summarization jobs via OpenAI's Batch API to halve the per-token cost versus real-time calls.

techniques.name: Code Mode / Tool-Call Compression
techniques.description: Lets the model emit compact code or structured calls instead of verbose natural-language tool invocations, shrinking both input and output token footprint in agentic workflows. Stacked on caching, it can cut input tokens by an order of magnitude.
techniques.savings: Up to 10x reduction in input tokens for agent workloads
techniques.example: Replace a 2,000-token JSON tool schema repeated every turn with a compact code-execution interface, combined with prompt + semantic caching, for agent loops.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Observability
techniques.description: Instruments every call to track token usage, cost per endpoint, cache hit rate, and model distribution—exposing waste that the other four levers can then target. You cannot optimize what you cannot measure.
techniques.savings: Enables 10-30% indirect savings by surfacing waste
techniques.example: Drop Helicone or Langfuse in as a proxy to see that one misconfigured endpoint is consuming 40% of spend, then fix it.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores LLM responses and returns cached answers for semantically similar queries, reducing both cost and latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; self-hosted infra costs only)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering model routing, fallback, load balancing, caching, and spend tracking behind one OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; Enterprise tier from ~$250/month for SSO, audit logs, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and proxy platform providing per-request cost/token monitoring, caching, rate limiting, and analytics with a one-line integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Pro from $20/user/month; usage-based tiers above free 10k requests/month

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store offering exact-match and vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses and embeddings, enabling multi-tier caching strategies at low latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis open source free; Redis Cloud from ~$5/month, scaling with memory/throughput

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Orchestration framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), prompt templating, and routing primitives for building optimized LLM apps.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from $39/user/month

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM observability and analytics platform tracking token usage, cost, latency, and cache performance across traces.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway pairing semantic caching with provider-native prompt caching and supporting Code Mode to reduce input tokens by an order of magnitude.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source; managed/enterprise pricing on request

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression toolkit that shortens prompts and RAG context (up to ~20x in extreme cases) while preserving task performance.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace routing requests across hundreds of models/providers with automatic price-based routing and fallback for cost optimization.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-use at provider cost plus small margin; no subscription

quick_wins: Enable native prompt caching and reorder prompts so the static system prompt and RAG context sit at the very front—up to 90% off cached input tokens with zero quality change.
Set max_tokens and instruct concise/JSON-only responses to cut expensive output tokens (4-5x the input price) by up to 50%.
Route easy queries to a budget-tier model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) and reserve flagship models for hard tasks—16x cheaper per identical token for simple workloads.
Drop in an observability proxy like Helicone or Langfuse to see exactly where tokens and dollars are going before optimizing anything.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive chatbot/FAQ traffic to eliminate 30-45% of requests entirely.
